concept.title: Images and Links in the Visual Editor
concept.shortdesc: Insert, paste, drop and resize images, and link to elements, keys, topics or web addresses from a picker — without typing paths or IDs.

section.title: Inserting Images
section.p: The Image button in the toolbar, or Image in the right-click menu, inserts an image where the document type allows it:

dlentry.dd: A <fig> with the image and an empty title for the caption.

section.p: You pick the file, then type its alternative text, written as an <alt> element. The href is relative to the topic.

ul.li: Paste an image (a screenshot): it is saved next to the topic — in images/, named <topic>-1.png… (setting ditacraft.imagePasteFolder) — and inserted on its own line.
Drop image files from VS Code's Explorer (hold Shift while dropping): they are linked where you drop them.
On an image: Replace image…, Alternative text…, and its size, placement and alignment in the .

section.title: Resizing Images

fig.title: A selected image, its resize handle and its attributes

image.alt: A diagram given by a key, selected on the page with a resize handle on its corner; the Properties view in the side bar shows keyref sync-diagram.

section.p: Images show at their size, alignment and placement. An image given by a key (keyref) shows the file the key points to.

section.title: Inserting Links
section.p: The Link button in the toolbar, Ctrl+K, or Link… in the right-click menu opens the link picker. Type to search:

image.alt: The link picker listing elements of this topic, keys of the root map, topics and maps of the workspace, and Web address.

dlentry.dd: The topic and its elements with an @id: href="#topic/element".
The keys of the root map, with their title and file: keyref="key".
Those of the workspace; choosing a topic then offers the topic itself or one of its elements: href="install.dita#install/prereq".
Or type the address straight in the search box: href="https://…" scope="external" format="html".

section.p: With text selected, the text becomes the link's text. Otherwise an empty link is inserted — when published, its text is the target's title; on the page it already shows that title, and follows it when the title changes.
On a link, the same command is Change link target… (only the target changes). The right-click menu also offers Open link target and Remove link (its text stays).
